known_MOS_source: First-study confirmation, nominal condition; explicitly known development evidence
passive_semantics: Synthetic equal-weight two-point log errors. Common: ln(Rs/Rs0)=ln(Rd/Rd0)=c. Ratio: ln(Rs/Rs0)=d/2, ln(Rd/Rd0)=-d/2. This is not a foundry/passive distribution or an APM Local extension.
decision: Test whether the lower MOS-error floor of R75 survives common error and whether larger ratio sensitivity reverses the ranking across the estimated break-even region.
prediction: Save both nominal-gradient and previously measured per-MOS-OP gradient predictions before new passive-condition targets. Known baseline output is allowed and disclosed; no target-condition OP enters predictions.
measurements: ads.passive-study.v1 with unchanged first-study DC/AC gain, center, bandwidth and current assessment; actual resistor and MOS readbacks plus KCL. No new sine/noise coverage from this block.
outcomes: Signed center error, MAE, RMS and per-index equal-weight squared loss across the two passive signs. Preserve all numerical and supported physical failures. Do not performance-filter the accuracy comparison.
sample_size_reason: The complete existing 464-coordinate finite cohort supplies the baseline moments used by this conditional comparison. Using every retained resistor circuit avoids subset selection; it is not a universal quota or a fresh population confirmation.
uncertainty: The exact finite-cohort contrast answers this synthetic transfer test. Do not describe it as new independent population confirmation or manufacturing yield. Any resampling of this known cohort is exploratory uncertainty only.
stopping: Exactly 2 candidates x 464 saved physical circuits x 6 conditions = 5568 attempts, once each. Three consecutive numerical failures stop the block for diagnosis. Required retries use identical saved inputs in new destinations and remain explicitly recorded; no automatic redraw or extension.
resource_bound: One native worker; estimated under 20 minutes and about 1.5 GiB native data from measured pilot. No new acquisition after 2026-09-13T19:56:10Z.
